title: Multiple inheritance

youtube.title: C++ Multiple Inheritance and the Diamond Problem | C++ Programming EP 67
youtube.description: In this episode you will inherit from two bases, explain the diamond problem and fix it with virtual inheritance, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Multiple inheritance · 0:51 Two bases · 1:31 The diamond · 2:01 Second program · 3:01 Recap · 3:31 Bug of the Day · 4:19 Challenge · 4:39 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "THE DIAMOND" in tomato on pastel blue; Xecxec next to a diamond made of four classes; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a diamond made of four classes

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today a class gets two parents. This is powerful, but it brings the famous diamond problem.

scenes.onScreen: "Multiple inheritance": numbered lines (1. A class can have several bases; 2. Two bases may have the same member name; 3. Virtual inheritance keeps one shared base) and an analogy card: a child with two parents: both may have a family car, so which car is meant?
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: C plus plus lets a class inherit from more than one base. List them with commas. If both bases have a member with the same name, a call is ambiguous. You must say which one you mean. The diamond problem appears when two bases share one grandparent. Then the object holds two copies of it. Virtual inheritance keeps only one.
points: A class can have several bases
Two bases may have the same member name
Virtual inheritance keeps one shared base

analogy.title: Multiple inheritance
analogy.body: A child with two parents: both may have a family car, so which car is meant?

scenes.onScreen: two.cpp: a class that inherits from two bases
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 4] Walker has a walk function. [HL 9] Swimmer has a swim function. [HL 14] Duck inherits from both. A comma separates the bases. [HL 18] A duck can walk. [HL 19] A duck can swim. The names are different, so there is no problem.

scenes.animation: Nodes pop in one by one; edges draw on as the narrator mentions them
scenes.narration: Look at the diamond. Animal is the grandparent. Walker and Swimmer both inherit from Animal. Duck inherits from both of them. Without care, a Duck would hold two Animal parts, one through each parent.

scenes.onScreen: diamond.cpp: virtual keeps one shared Animal part
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 4] Animal has one member, legs. [HL 9] The word virtual tells the compiler to share one Animal part. [HL 10] Swimmer does the same. [HL 11] Duck has only one Animal part. [HL 15] So the name legs is not ambiguous. We can use it directly. [HL 16] The output is four.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as diamond dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints four.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A class can inherit from several bases. Two. Equal member names in two bases make a call ambiguous. Three. The diamond gives two copies of the grandparent. Four. Virtual inheritance keeps one copy. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A class can inherit from several bases.
Equal member names in two bases make a call ambiguous.
The diamond gives two copies of the grandparent.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: An ambiguous member
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Both bases have a hello function. The call on C says hello, and the compiler says the request for hello is ambiguous. It cannot guess. Write the base name and two colons to choose.

scenes.onScreen: A diamond is forever. So is the ambiguity, until you add virtual.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: A diamond is forever. So is the ambiguity, until you add virtual.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Make two base classes with the same function name. Inherit from both, and call each version. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: composition and slicing. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

two.cpp: In function 'int main()':
two.cpp:18:7: error: request for member 'hello' is ambiguous
   18 |     c.hello();
      |       ^~~~~
two.cpp:11:10: note: candidates are: 'void B::hello() const'
   11 |     void hello() const { cout << "B" << endl; }
bug.why: Both bases offer hello, so the compiler cannot guess. Write the name of the base and two colons to choose one.

pun: "A diamond is forever. So is the ambiguity, until you add virtual."
challenge: Make two base classes with the same function name. Inherit from both, and call each version.
challengeAnswer: Write the base name, two colons, and the function name. Call a colon colon hello, and then b colon colon hello.
